The strongest ground is that the debt was barred by the statute of limitations on July 1, and in jurisdictions that require a signed writing to revive a barred debt, the oral promise cannot revive it. Lack of consideration is weaker, because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 makes a promise to pay a time-barred debt enforceable without new consideration, and the "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor creates duress. The idea that the debt was wholly extinguished is also off, since the limitations period usually bars the remedy rather than the debt itself.

CONFIDENCE: 60
